newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen to close last "filthiest fuel" power station.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen to close last "filthiest fuel" power station.

text.p: PowerGen Plc, Britian's second biggest generator, said on Wednesday it was closing the last of its power stations to burn Orimulsion, dubbed the world's filthiest fuel.
PowerGen said it would try to redeploy the 41 staff employed at the 500 megawatt Ince plant in northwest England plant, or seek voluntary redundancies.

The closure of Ince marks the end of PowerGen's current dealings with Orimulsion, a cheap fuel from Venezuela that has triggered attacks from environmentalists and legal action from a car firm that alleged fallout damaged paintwork on new cars.
"The Ince closure will follow the ending of the five-year Orimulsion contract for Ince which will not be renewed," PowerGen said in a statement.
The company said the power station, near Chester, would stop generating electricity at the end of next March.
To make up for the loss of power, PowerGen will start up a generating unit at Fiddler's Ferry power station in Warrington, also in northwest England.
The unit was placed in reserve in March 1994 and should return to commercial operating in December.

PoweGen closed its Richborough power plant in Kent, south east England in March. Richborough was the only other of its three originally oil-fired power stations that had been adapted to burn Orimulsion.
